      Hundreds more homes set for part of Leicestershire in major planning update

      One part of Leicestershire will get many new houses - and a country park

      Comments2
      News
      Tess Rushin Local Democracy Reporter
      06:00, 07 Oct 2026
      Listen to audio version of this article
      Sponsored by
      0:00 / 5:49
      Instaread

      Hundreds more homes are set for part of Leicestershire after councillors greenlit a number of schemes.

      ‌

      Officials on Blaby District Council’s (BDC) planning committee gave the major housing boost to the area last week, with more than 700 homes in total now approved for construction.

      ‌

      However, these plans, which include nearly 350 for Blaby itself, have proved highly controversial with residents, with flooding fears and infrastructure concerns repeatedly raised.

      ‌

      Despite those worries, the plans were approved. More details on the schemes can be found below:

      Teaching assistant who supported countless children named as victim of fatal Hinckley crash

      Road closed after huge Birstall fire lights up night sky

      345 homes in Blaby

      A two-part application approved by BDC was Bonnel Homes and Woods Hardwick’s development of 345 homes and a country park at Keepers Farm, off Winchester Road, in Blaby.

      The first half of the scheme was for full permission for 77 houses – including 20 affordable homes – office/shop space, and associated demolition work on the land.

      ‌

      BDC also gave outline permission for the second half of the scheme – up to 268 houses, including 67 affordable homes – as well as an 8.47-hectare country park – for Keepers Farm.

      The Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) spoke to people living in the area of the planned 345 homes before the meeting took place.

      ‌

      Marie and Rob Amey live on Winchester Road and were worried that infrastructure wouldn’t cope, claiming traffic in the area was already “horrendous”.

      Blaby Parish Councillor Sue Jordan spoke out about the application at the meeting. She said: “The village has accommodated significant residential development in recent years and has contributed substantially towards meeting local housing needs.

      “In the parish council’s views there is no demonstrable justification for imposing further large scale housing development in the village, particularly when existing [housing] targets have already been surpassed.

      ‌

      “The submitted transport assessment acknowledges that the proposed development would generate considerable additional vehicle movements. Blaby already experiences significant traffic congestion on the main routes entering and leaving the village, particularly during peak commuting periods. Winchester Road especially at school is chockablock already without all these extra houses on it.”

      In its latest advice, Leicestershire County Council, acting as the local highways authority, said: “The impacts of the development on highway safety would not be unacceptable, and when considered cumulatively with other developments, the impacts on the road network would not be severe.”

      Despite the concerns raised, the application was unanimously approved, subject to 43 conditions for the full application and 39 conditions for the outline application.

      ‌

      180 homes in Cosby

      Residents in Cosby were opposed to the building of 180 homes the village due to flooding fears.

      The application, which has now been approved, would see a new vehicle access from Broughton Road, and an extension to existing allotments, alongside the homes.

      However great concern was raised by residents living in Cosby’s Elm Tree Road, with some properties’ gardens backing onto the development site.

      ‌

      Nigel Beeby was one of the neighbours whose Elm Tree Road property backed onto the proposed development.

      The 59-year-old told the LDRS: “I’m very disappointed [with the plans]. There’s already flooding in this area, it flows off the fields.

      ‌

      Cosby and South Whetstone ward councillor Les Phillimore spoke against the plans at the BDC meeting.

      He said: “We all remain deeply concerned about the access and egress to the proposed development, the impact on Broughton Road, which is inherently a one-way area, due to on-street parking, and I concur with everyone who has ever commented the proposed mini roundabout is farcical and will inherently be ridden over.

      “I’m aware the parish council requested the county highways case officer meet on site to discuss the concerns. For whatever reason that request was not taken up in preference to quite a lengthy email response.

      ‌

      “Members at the planning committee on the 30th July, you rightly deferred the application for further highways information. To paraphrase my ward partner, if nothing has changed with the proposals for the highway, how can the committee approve the application when you were unable to determine it on the first consideration?”

      On the latest plans, Leicestershire County Council acting as the local highways authority and local lead flood authority asked for further information regarding the development which has now been satisfied and both authorities have no objections subject to conditions.

      The plans were approved, subject to 25 conditions.

      ‌

      180 homes in Sapcote

      Another 180 homes on a 10.12 hectare site were approved on land west of Park Road and south of West Field Road in Sapcote at the same BDC meeting.

      The application, by Miller Homes and Hallam Land, also included highways improvements including access from West Field Road and Park Road, on-site open space and a small parking area for All Saints Primary School.

      Plans noted the site consisted of three agricultural fields, and the development will form an extension to the south of the existing 125 Miller Homes development.

      ‌

      Of the 125 homes, 23 will be one-storey and the remaining 157 will be two-storeys in height. A total of 45 will be affordable housing.

      However, 25 letters of objection were received, with concerns including flooding, drainage, highways and parking infrastructure.

      In its consultation response, Leicestershire County Council, acting as the local highways authority said: “The impacts of the development on highway safety would not be unacceptable, and when considered cumulatively with other developments, the impacts on the road network would not be severe.

      Article continues below

      The committee voted unanimously in approval of the application.
